sanskrit_verse:
अधिविन्ना तु भर्तव्या महदेनोऽन्यथा भवेत् ।
यत्रानुकूल्यं दम्पत्योस्त्रिवर्गस्तत्र वर्धते ॥७४॥
transliteration: adhivinnā tu bhartavyā mahad eno 'nyathā bhavet / yatrānukūlyaṃ damapatyostrivargastatra vardhate // YajñS_1.74 //
sph_interpretive_translation: When mutual harmony prevails between spouses, all three aims of life—Dharma, Artha, Kama—are fulfilled; without it, great loss occurs.
jurisprudential_principles: Capacity-based responsibility is shared in union
executable_legal_axioms: IF spousal alignment = true THEN tri-varga fulfillment = true
IF spousal disharmony = true THEN dharma-artha-kama degradation = true
IF mutual cooperation = absent THEN legal capacity = diminished
IF relationship integrity = restored THEN societal dharma = increased
supreme_court_application: In matrimonial disputes, the Supreme Court shall assess the degree of alignment and cooperative intent between partners as the primary indicator of dharmic order, not fault or blame.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramana reveals that disharmony causes sequential diminishment of purpose. Thus, restoration follows from re-establishing alignment rather than assigning punitive consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Assign completion practices for unresolved emotional residues
Reaffirm shared intention for mutual upliftment
Restore energetic coherence through synchronized rituals
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Harmony between spouses ensures expansion of Dharma, Artha, and Kama. There is no punishment here—only the natural law of consequence and the path of restoration. Consciousness alone is the ultimate judge.
